title: The Capacity Calculator: Find the Money Gap to 75% Billable Utilization
description: A Google Sheets capacity calculator: enter team size, hours and rate to see your utilization and the money gap to 75%. Plus how to close the gap.
lead: This is the full Capacity Calculator from the carousel. Enter your team size, hours and rate, and see your billable utilization and the money gap to 75%. This guide gives you the sheet with every formula, a 2-week time tracking plan and how to price on the hours you really bill.
insider: Unbilled hours often mean not enough work coming in, not a lazy team. In our 5-day blitz we booked **25 calls in one week** for a client from 96,408 emails. Closing the utilization gap starts with a full pipeline, and filling it every day is what we do for clients.

blocks.text: The numbers behind the carousel

[SPI Research's 2026 Professional Services Maturity Benchmark](https://www.deltek.com/resources/articles/professional-services-billable-utilization-historic-low/), published with Deltek, found billable utilization hit **66.4%**, its lowest point in nearly two decades. In 2021 it was **73.2%**.

items: **Top firms bill more.** High-performance firms billed **75.0%** of their time. Everyone else billed **64.9%**.
**Profit is thin.** Industry EBITDA was **9.9%** in 2025, well below SPI's expected **15%** benchmark.

**75% is the target.** [Deltek's summary](https://www.deltek.com/resources/articles/professional-services-benchmarks/) calls 75% the threshold SPI considers optimal. The survey covered over 500 firms.

blocks.text: **Utilization** means: billable hours ÷ total available hours. If a person works 40 hours and bills 26, their utilization is 65%.
Why this is a money problem, not a time problem

Every hour you don't bill still costs you the same salary, rent and tools. Going from 66.4% to 75% means billing about 3.4 more hours per person per week at a 40-hour week. You don't need more hours. You need more of the same hours to be paid for.
The Capacity Calculator (Google Sheets)
Open a new Google Sheet. Put the labels in column A and the values or formulas in column B, starting in row 2. You type values only in B2 to B8. The rest calculate.

blocks.label: Formatting
blocks.text: Format B7 and B11 as percent, B6, B8, B14, B16 and B17 as currency. Rows 9 to 17 should never be typed over.
Worked example (the carousel math)

items: Capacity: 5 people × 40 hours × 48 weeks = **9,600 hours** a year.
Money: 826 × $100 = **$82,600** a year (the sheet shows $82,560 because it doesn't round the hours).
Per person: 825.6 ÷ 5 ÷ 48 = about **3.4 extra billable hours a week**.

blocks.text: Step 1: Count real billable hours

A 40-hour week is never 40 billable hours. Email, meetings, sales and admin take time. A common rule is to plan on **75%**, so 40 hours is really about 30 billable. Use 30, not 40, for planning and pricing.
Step 2: Track every hour for 2 weeks
You can't fix what you guess. For 2 weeks, everyone logs every hour into one of these buckets. A free time tracker or a shared sheet works.
Add up the client work hours, divide by 2 to get a weekly number, then divide by the number of people. That's your value for cell B5.
Step 3: Cut the non-billable

Look at the biggest non-billable bucket first. Example: 5 one-hour internal meetings a week is **5 hours a week** per person. Turning 3 of them into a written update gives back 3 hours, almost the whole 3.4-hour gap in the example.

head: Problem you find
Fix

A clear scope with priced extras (see our [SCOPE guide](/guides/scope.html))

Not enough client work to fill hours
A pipeline problem: more sales conversations, not more effort

blocks.text: Step 4: Price on the hours you bill
If you set your rate by dividing cost by 40 hours, you are under-pricing. Divide by the billable hours instead.
Pricing on 40 hours sets break-even 25% too low ($37.50 vs $50). Every hour you can't bill eats your profit.

blocks.label: The rule
blocks.text: You don't need more hours. You need more of them billed.

resources.name: Deltek: billable utilization hits a historic low
resources.note: SPI Research 2026 benchmark: 66.4%, 73.2% in 2021, 75.0% vs 64.9%, EBITDA 9.9%

faq.a: It's the level SPI Research considers optimal for professional services firms. Very senior people and owners often bill less because they sell and manage. Set a target per role if you need to.

faq.q: Should I count sales calls as billable?
faq.a: No. They're important, but no client pays for them. Track them in their own bucket so you can see how much time sales really takes.
Then focus on price: make sure your rate is set on billable hours, not 40. Going much higher than 75% often leads to burnout.

faq.q: Why does the sheet show $82,560 and the carousel $82,600?
faq.a: The carousel rounds the hour gap to 826 hours before multiplying by $100. The sheet uses the exact 825.6 hours.
